properties.title: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued May 30 at 10:48PM MDT until May 30 at 11:00PM MDT by NWS Rapid City SD
properties.description:
At 1048 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 3 miles east of
Billsburg, or 25 miles north of Philip, moving northeast at 20 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Milesville.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued May 30 at 11:48PM CDT until May 31 at 5:00AM CDT by NWS Hastings NE
properties.description:
FFWGID

The National Weather Service in Hastings has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Osborne County in north central Kansas...

* Until 500 AM CDT.

* At 1148 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 3 and 4 inches of rain
have fallen over the last few hours in parts of the Warning area.
Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the
warned area tonight before rain likely ends within the next hour
or so. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses as well as
other poor drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
mainly rural areas of Southeastern Osborne County

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Wolf Creek, Carr Creek, Center Twin Creek, Coon Creek, Fourmile
Creek, Indian Creek, North Branch Spillman Creek, East Fork Wolf
Creek, Twin Creek and East Twin Creek.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued May 30 at 11:41PM CDT by NWS Aberdeen SD
properties.description:

miles north of Draper, or 14 miles northeast of Murdo, moving
northwest at 40 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and nickel size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Draper, Brown Church, Hayes, Wendte, Van Metre, and Chantier Creek
Recreation Area.
properties.instruction: If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued May 30 at 10:35PM MDT until May 31 at 1:30AM MDT by NWS Billings MT
properties.description:
FFWBYZ

The National Weather Service in Billings has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Northern Elk Burn Area in...
Northwestern Sheridan County in north central Wyoming...

* Until 130 AM MDT.

* At 1035 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Northern Elk Burn Area. Between 0.7 and 1.2
inches of rain have fallen a few miles west of Parkman. Additional
rainfall is occurring. Flash flooding and debris flow is expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding and debris flow caused by thunderstorms in
and around the Northern Elk Burn Area.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flooding of areas in and downstream of the Northern Elk
Burn Area...mainly on northeast side of burn area.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Parkman.
properties.instruction:
Life threatening flooding of creeks, roads, and normally dry coulees
in and downstream of the Northern Elk burn area is likely. In
addition to the flash flooding, the heavy rains may trigger
rockslides, mudslides, and debris flows in steep terrain.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.description:

East Fork White River at Seymour.

Shoals gage reading is over 17 feet.  Private levees may be
overtopped in many cases.

- At 9:45 PM EDT Saturday /8:45 PM CDT Saturday/ the stage was
19.3 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours
ending at 9:45 PM EDT Saturday /8:45 PM CDT Saturday/ was
19.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 19.6
feet just after midnight tonight. It will then fall below
flood stage Monday evening.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
